I.title: Audit denial does not enforce the planned stop boundary
I.evidence: audit_hook increments denied_operations, writes a row and raises PermissionError. The child has no denied_operations check after imports, before READY, or before advancing from PCSC to ETEAC. The only later consumption is supervisor blocked_operations collection after exit/cap (414-424). Native runner.git_sha (1456-1466) catches Exception, illustrating that an exception from an audit hook need not escape product code; its presently allowed exact invocation is not itself a denied event.
I.impact: If a library or product path catches a denied-operation exception, the attempt can continue through product work or advance to ETEAC despite R396 requiring stop-and-report on any denied operation. Operation denial itself remains effective; the defect is continuation after a mandatory stop, not a demonstrated network escape.
I.recommendation: Obtain the next actual Astra plan before changing the driver. Provide a driver-owned fail-stop mechanism for denied operations that is independent of whether native product code catches PermissionError, preserves the denial record and still lets the supervisor own cleanup. Do not change product functions or retry this attempt.
